title: Anxiety, Depression, and School Pressure: When to Seek Help
summary: The pre-adolescent stage brings pressures: school, friends, self-image, and physical changes. Warning signs: sadness lasting more than two weeks, withdrawal, academic decline, changes in sleep or appetite, or thoughts of harm. Parents: listen without judgment, reassure them: "I am with you, we will solve this together." Consult a pediatrician or mental health specialist early.
try_this: Create a "Weekly Mood Scale": a simple chart (1-10) for mood, energy, and sleep. Review it together monthly. If the curve declines for more than two weeks, consult a specialist.
reflection_prompts: What was the highest/lowest point on the mood scale this month?

review_defects.why: The Arabic specifies 'psychologist' (أخصائي نفسي), while the English uses the broader term 'mental health specialist', which could include psychiatrists, therapists, etc. This loses specificity.
